At that standoff the teapot's body/rim sits right on the mug's rim at the carry goal, and during the 95-degree tilt the swinging body sweeps straight through the mug, so no collision-free goal or path existed (the carry goal also had to be a valid start for the pour path, so both shared the same too-low band). Raising the above-terms one step to 'small' clearance on the carry subgoal and on both the pour path and pour subgoal keeps the spout centered over the opening and keeps the bands mutually consistent for stage-to-stage continuity, while lifting the pot enough for its body to clear the mug's rim through the tilt.

failure.message: no transport goal is a start the pour accepts

rounds.diagnosis: The pour was specified with the spout tip held only a small standoff (about 1-3 cm) over the mug opening. As the pot tips forward about its lateral axis to bring teapot.+front down, the spout and the pot body sweep through the mug rim at that height, so no collision-free goal or tilting motion exists inside the band; the tight centering of the spout during the swing also leaves no room for the compensating translation the tilt needs. Stepping the above-mug clearance from small to medium on the pour path and subgoal lifts the whole band away from the rim (keeping the pour aimed into the mug) and relaxing the path centering term to loose gives the spout room to arc while the pot rotates. The carry stage's standoff is widened the same step so its goal still lies inside the pour stage's path region and the stages remain connected.
